summary:
R3's SP category is the number to build around today — 98-75 (57%) over the last 14 days, its best mark of any rating/category cell and a clean improvement over its own 53% season SP baseline. That's meaningful because four of today's seven games carry full four-way consensus, and three of those are pitching-mismatch spots where the SP signal should carry weight: MIL @ NYM (Misiorowski vs Manaea, model unanimous on MIL by -2.56 to -2.99), HOU @ NYY (Wesneski vs Cole, unanimous NYY at +2.34 to +2.81), and BAL @ STL (Rogers vs TBD, unanimous BAL). R3 also leads all ratings in recent strong-play profitability — 24-10 (71%, +20.0u) over the last 7 days and 44-31 (59%, +16.0u) over 14 — so when R3's number is the largest in the group, as it is in the NYY and MIL games, that's the side to lean hardest on.

The three split games — COL @ WSN, ARI @ SFG, LAD @ ATL — are exactly where you'd expect noise, since none clear a full point of delta and none have full consensus; treat those as pass or small-stake spots rather than model-driven plays. Notice also that LAD is on today's board, and LAD ranks among the model's most reliable picks-when-liked historically (22-10, 69%, strong 16-3 at +18.0u), but today the rating disagrees with itself (R4 favors LAD, R1-R3 lean ATL), so that team strength doesn't apply here — the pick is ATL, not LAD, so don't let the team's name override the split signal. KCR @ TOR is unanimous but thin (deltas -0.62 to -1.12), so size down relative to the MIL and NYY spots. Across the board, trends+sp remains the most reliable combo (56.5%, n=421), and today's biggest-consensus games are exactly the ones where SP is doing the heavy lifting — lean into R3 and R1 there, and keep KCR/BAL as secondary plays given smaller edges.
